text:
Marathon Petroleum has fallen 3.5% today and 14.9% over two weeks amid mounting geopolitical risk in the Middle East and signs of refining headwinds. The immediate trigger appears to be escalating attacks on oil infrastructure—Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabian facilities, Iranian tanker incidents in the Strait of Hormuz, and Ukraine's ongoing targeting of Russian refineries—which create supply uncertainty without yet pulling crude prices decisively higher (US oil at $89.53/barrel, down from earlier levels in the month). Meanwhile, U.S. refineries are running at 95.7% capacity with gasoline and diesel stockpiles elevated, which limits margin expansion for domestic refiners even if geopolitical disruptions tighten global markets.

The stock's weakness also reflects a broader two-week decline that started before today's latest headlines, suggesting investors have been pricing in the risk of Middle East escalation and reduced refining profitability as inventories build. With U.S. oil prices stable but not spiking despite regional threats, refiners face pressure on both the input (crude) and output (fuel margins) sides of the business right now.
